A reference set to score arms against

Source: R/core-bench-reference.R
hr_reference.Rd

A reference holds the items a benchmark runs every arm on, the label each item is scored against, the cluster it belongs to (the unit whose items share errors, such as a document or a task), and the split it is in.

Usage

hr_reference(
  items,
  labels,
  cluster,
  split = c("dev", "exploratory", "calibration", "test", "final"),
  inclusion_prob = 1,
  strata = NULL,
  coders = NULL
)

hr_reference_add(
  reference,
  items,
  labels,
  cluster,
  split = c("dev", "exploratory", "calibration", "test", "final"),
  inclusion_prob = 1,
  strata = NULL,
  coders = NULL
)

Arguments

items

The items, one per element: a named list whose names are the item ids and whose elements are the payloads the arms are given (any R object: a question, a question with a file path, a record), a named character vector (names are ids, values payloads), or an unnamed character vector of ids, which are then their own payloads.

labels

The label of each item, one per item: an atomic vector, or a list whose elements may hold several accepted answers. NA for an item with no label, which is scored NA. Unnamed, the labels go to the items in order; named, they go to the items by name, and the names must be the item ids. The same holds for cluster, split, inclusion_prob and strata when they give one value per item.

cluster

The cluster of each item, one per item, or one value for all. Taken as text.

split

The split of each item, one per item, or one value for all: "dev", "exploratory", "calibration", "test" or "final". When split is not given, every item goes in "dev".

inclusion_prob

The probability each item was drawn into the reference, in (0, 1]: one per item or one for all.

strata

The sampling stratum of each item, or NULL.

coders

The labels individual coders gave, one row per item and one column per coder (a matrix or data frame), or NULL.

reference

An hr_reference.

Value

An object of class hr_reference: a list of ids, items (the payloads, named by id), labels, cluster, split, inclusion_prob, strata, coders and hash. hr_reference_add() returns a new reference holding the old items and the new ones, sharing the old one's lock.

Details

The splits keep tuning apart from evidence. "dev" is for tuning prompts and thresholds, and hr_benchmark() marks its rows as not reportable. "exploratory" is for early experiments kept out of the test set, "calibration" for setting signal thresholds, "test" for the reported comparison, and "final" for a held-out set run once per release.

inclusion_prob is the probability with which each item was drawn into the reference, for estimates that weight items by it (see hr_ht_estimate()); 1 means every item of the population is in the reference.

A reference is locked when a benchmark starts scoring it. After that hr_reference_add() refuses to add items to it or to any reference built from it, with an error of class hr_reference_locked, so gold items cannot be chosen after the results are seen. The lock is shared by every copy of the reference. The hash is a SHA-256 hash of the ids, payloads, labels, clusters, splits, inclusion probabilities, strata and coders; hr_benchmark() refuses a reference whose content no longer matches it.

See also

hr_benchmark(), hr_arm()

Other harness: gr_arm(), gr_qa_reference(), gr_scorer_answer(), hr_arm(), hr_benchmark(), hr_contrast(), hr_drift_check(), hr_mdd(), hr_report(), hr_scorer()

Examples

ref <- hr_reference(
  items = list(q1 = "Capital of France?", q2 = "Capital of Peru?",
               q3 = "Capital of Chad?"),
  labels = c("Paris", "Lima", "N'Djamena"),
  cluster = c("europe", "americas", "africa"),
  split = "test")
ref
#> <hr_reference> 3 item(s) in 3 cluster(s)
#>   splits: test 3 
#>   hash: 14e0a94eaaec

# Items can be added until a benchmark has scored the reference.
ref <- hr_reference_add(ref, list(q4 = "Capital of Fiji?"), "Suva", "oceania",
                        split = "test")
length(ref$ids)
#> [1] 4
